name: Euro-area economy
summary: Eurostat puts euro-area Q3 GDP growth at 0.4%; October composite PMI 51.7, above 50; November flash PMI due later
state: Eurostat's flash estimate of 30 Oct put euro-area GDP growth at 0.4% in the third quarter and 0.5% in the EU (Eurostat). The final HCOB composite PMI for October was 51.7, a four-month low but above 50. Both readings sit above the Normal lines; searches on 15 Nov found no newer data, and November flash PMIs are due later in the month.
for_you: Euro-area growth is positive, so there is no broad downturn in the region for now. Exporters and workers in energy-intensive industries remain the most exposed to higher energy costs from the Middle East conflict.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% (positive) and composite PMI 51.7 > 50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
Il Sole 24 Ore — Eurozone GDP grows by 0.4 per cent in the third quarter

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
